name: Ui_ProfileWindow_BuildTitleRows
summary: Builds the title rows of the profile card: for every unlocked title flag it binds a left/right text pair through vtable+0x34 and then composes and applies the 'title_d' heading with the number of unlocked titles.
evidence: The body binds the literals txt_l1/txt_r1/r2/r3 and the eight g_00464070 pane pointers, gated by the work flags f_2A678 bits 1/2/4/8, and the callees are now named Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor/Ui_AnimRef_Bind/Ui_LayoutRef_Release; the same flag word is read by Ui_ProfileWindow_RefreshStats (0x0046408C).

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseChildren
summary: Release/teardown helper of a large message-style window: stores the class vtable, drops the handles at +0x2078/+0x207C and walks the child chain at +0x20D0 releasing message pages, two text elements, a panel and the animation object. Used when the window is destroyed or its page set is replaced.
evidence: No named caller or constructor in the merged tree shares it, so the 'MessageWindow' class label remains a layout guess; the mechanism (vtable store + child-chain release) is certain. 0x003B1234 is a byte copy.

name: maybe_Ui_PagedTextWindow_InitRows
summary: Creates the five text rows and the 'next' icons of a paged text/memo window, builds the long-text layout for the body and selects the page indicator variant (2/3 rows) from the entry flags.
evidence: The body binds null_txt_l0/icon_next_0/null_txt_r1_0..r5_0 and drives them through the layout factory (Ui_AnimRef*/Ui_LayoutRef_Release), then calls func_001A61FC(self,0,2 or 3). It is called on an embedded object at +0x70 by maybe_Ui_PopupWindow_InitPanes (0x00403D88) and from the ambiguous 0x0066D398 thunk, so 'PagedTextWindow' is plausible but the owning class and the real argument count (the thunk forwards four registers) are still open.

name: Ui_Drawable_Dtor
summary: Non-deleting destructor of the base 2D drawable widget: tears the widget tree down in reverse member order (the 0xD88 refcounted block, the 0x3C intrusive list, three list heads, the 0x54/0x84 list nodes, three 0x50 containers, the 0x330 container array, the 0xD30 reference and the 0x148 sub-object at 0x001D8C2C).
evidence: Shares vtable 0x0075C248 with the already-named Ui_Drawable_DtorDelete (0x002CF634) and with Ui_Drawable_ReleaseMembers (0x002CF9BE), i.e. the same class family, and 0x0030FF0C ends by calling it on the base at -0xE78.

name: maybe_Ui_BigScreen_Dtor

evidence: The pair 0x0030FEFC/0x0030FF0C and the ctor 0x0030F590 agree on every member offset, but all three names carry maybe_ and no third named function shares the class vtable, so 'BigScreen' is still a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_ReleaseChildren

evidence: Only the deleting dtor 0x003BE534 refers to it, and that name is itself a maybe_; no third named function shares the vtables, so both the class and the 'ReleaseChildren' role stay unverified.

name: maybe_Ui_Drawable_ReleaseMembers

evidence: The body is a damaged decompilation (unaff_r4/r5/r7, dropped argument registers, one 'removing unreachable block' warning), so the exact member set cannot be confirmed even though it duplicates the tail of 0x002CF644 byte for byte; kept at low confidence because of the damage, not because the shape is doubtful.

evidence: Body is exactly Ui_LayoutRef_Release(self+0x13) + Ui_Object_DtorBase(-0x4C) + free, and its twin 0x0045F080 is the same without the free; the name's 'Small' only records the one-pane layout, which is verified.

name: Ui_Window_DtorSmall
summary: Non-deleting destructor twin of 0x0045F05C (no free).
evidence: Byte-for-byte 0x0045F05C minus func_0010F6CC, forming the standard deleting/non-deleting pair.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_DtorDeleteBig
summary: Deleting destructor of a large screen object: destroys the embedded widget array and the base, then frees.
evidence: No named ctor or vtable sibling; 'Big' only describes the array size.

name: Ui_ChildWindow_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a child-window object: destroys the 0x50-byte pane at +0x58, the base and frees.
evidence: Ui_LayoutRef_Release(self+0x2a) + one -0x50 step + Ui_Object_DtorBase(-0x58) + free; 0x0047C1B8 is the same body without the free, so the pair is verified and the label is deliberately generic.

name: Ui_ChildWindow_Dtor
summary: Non-deleting destructor of the same child-window object as 0x0047C18C.
evidence: Identical to 0x0047C18C minus func_0010F6CC.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_DtorDelete1
summary: Deleting destructor of a window object (copy 1): destroys its panes and the base, then frees.
evidence: Numeric suffix only; no class evidence.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_DtorDelete2
summary: Deleting destructor of a window object (copy 2): destroys its panes and the base, then frees.
evidence: Numeric suffix only; no class evidence.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_DtorDelete4Sub
summary: Deleting destructor of a window that owns four stacked 0x50-byte panes plus the 0x11C object; destroys them and frees.
evidence: The four-step teardown (0x54 then 3 x 0x50) matches the name's '4Sub', but no named ctor or vtable sibling identifies the class.

name: maybe_Ui_MessagePage_DtorDelete2
summary: Deleting destructor of a large message-page object: destroys the page at +0x1E18, stamps the panel vtables 0x75E540/0x77FCFC and releases the layout reference.
evidence: Damaged decompilation: the body ends in halt_baddata() and depends on in_ZR/in_CY, so more than half of the teardown is missing; only the first steps can be trusted.

name: maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_SubObjectDtor
signature: void maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_SubObjectDtor(void* self, void* vtable, UmaOwner* owner)
summary: Destructor of a sub-object of the 'uma' (horse) window: releases its panes and list and frees.
evidence: Only the deleting-dtor mechanism is verified; the horse-window link is inferred from the address region.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DeleteDtor_77DD50
summary: Deleting destructor of a one-pane widget: destroys the pane at +0x4C and the base, then frees; the caller passes the 0x77DD50 class vtable.
evidence: The body never references 0x77DD50 itself (the vtable arrives in arg2), so the class cannot be confirmed here; it is the same generated shape as 0x0045F05C.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_Dtor_77DD50
summary: Non-deleting destructor twin of 0x005931F0 (same one-pane teardown, no free).
evidence: Same body as 0x005931F0 minus func_0010F6CC; the 0x77DD50 class attribution comes from the caller, not the body.

name: maybe_Ui_ChildWidget_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a container widget that owns four 0x13C-byte child objects at +0x204: destroys them, releases the layout object at +0x14C and frees.
evidence: Vtable 0x007801B4 is also installed by Ui_WorldMap_CreateMarkerArray (0x00621DD4), but that ctor builds five 0x10-byte markers at +0x60, not four 0x13C objects, so the layout does not match and the class stays open.

name: maybe_Ui_CursorIcon_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a small cursor/icon container: stamps its vtable, releases the intrusive list and the 0x50-byte parts, then frees.
evidence: Its non-deleting twin 0x001D8558 is called by Ui_TimeWindow_Dtor as a sub-object dtor, so the role is right, but 'CursorIcon' is still the previous worker's guess (the sibling Ui_CursorIcon_* functions are not proven to be this class).

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DtorChain
summary: Non-deleting destructor of a widget with a long relative member chain: releases two panes, an object array and the list heads, and returns the enclosing pointer.
evidence: It calls the maybe_ helper Ui_Object_ReleaseArray and no named ctor shares its layout; 'DtorChain' only describes the shape.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_GetBasePointer
summary: Tiny helper that releases/returns the standard 0x50-byte pane chain and hands back the enclosing object pointer twelve bytes before it.
evidence: The single call (Ui_LayoutRef_Release with dropped arguments) plus 'return base-0xC' is the relative-pointer idiom every ctor in this range uses, but nothing identifies the owning class or proves it is a getter.

name: Ui_PaneSet_Dtor_2C
summary: Deleting destructor of a two-pane UI object variant: destroys the panes at +0x4C/+0x9C and the 0x148 sub-object, then frees.
evidence: Same generated family as 0x002E86E0/0x002D04C4 (two Ui_LayoutRef_Release steps 0x50 apart) with func_001D8C2C as the final member dtor; the count in the name matches.

name: maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_ResetState
summary: Resets an embedded window object: stores the new state at +0xB4, re-initialises the circular list head at +0xB8, copies the two-word descriptor 0x0072B384 and releases the two panes ahead of it.
evidence: The mechanism is clear, but no named caller or ctor proves the object is the shop window, and the release calls make 'ResetState' only partly descriptive.

name: maybe_Ui_TwoElementPanel_Ctor
summary: In-place constructor of an embedded two-element panel: stores the parent at +0xBC, links the circular list head at +0xC0, copies the element descriptor 0x0072B36C and releases the two pane slots.
evidence: The init part matches a two-element panel, but the two Ui_LayoutRef_Release calls are teardown work and no named caller confirms the class.

name: maybe_Ui_SingleElementPanel_Ctor
summary: In-place constructor of an embedded single-element panel: stores the parent at +0x5C, links the list head at +0x60 and copies the descriptor 0x0072B404.
evidence: Same construction idiom as 0x003A57A0 but with one element; no named caller or vtable sibling confirms the class.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelMessageWindow_TextDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a text object inside a panel message window: releases the layout at +0x11C and the base, then frees.
evidence: The body is a plain one-member dtor; 'PanelMessageWindow_TextDelete' is inferred from the neighbourhood only.

name: maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_Delete
summary: Destructor of a composite window instance: destroys the object and frees.
evidence: Only self-references; the 'CompositeWindow' family exists but nothing links this particular address to it.

name: maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_Release
summary: Non-deleting destructor of the same composite window instance as 0x003BEE4C.
evidence: Same body as 0x003BEE4C without the free; class link is still indirect (only 0x003BE534/0x003BE548 mention it, and both are maybe_).

name: maybe_Ui_SubWindow2_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of an embedded sub-window variant: one Ui_LayoutRef_Release step, the 0x11C member dtor and the free.
evidence: Mirrors 0x003E071C with a different offset; 'SubWindow2' is a copy index, not an identified class.

name: maybe_Ui_SubWindow2_Dtor
summary: Non-deleting destructor twin of 0x003E07EC.
evidence: Same body as 0x003E07EC minus the free; no class evidence.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_Dtor
signature: void maybe_Ui_Screen_Dtor(UiScreen* self, void* vtable, int owner)
summary: Destructor of a large screen object: destroys the embedded widget chain and frees.
evidence: No named ctor or vtable sibling; 'Screen' is a size/shape label.

name: maybe_Ui_StatCompare_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a stat-compare widget: destroys the two panes and the 0x11C sub-object, then frees.
evidence: The body matches the generic two-pane family and the name records the stat-compare UI region, but no named ctor shares the class vtable.

name: Container_List_InitAt5C
summary: Initialises an intrusive list inside a widget: sets the class pointer, makes the head at +0x5C self-linking, clears the count and copies the element descriptor.
evidence: Fully verified from the body (f_58 = vtable, f_60/f_64 = self+0x5C, f_68 = 0, descriptor from 0x0072...); the old name 'InitAt5C' described exactly the offset that the body writes.

name: Sound_InitPlayers
summary: Initialises the sound system's player/voice slots: allocates the per-voice structures and registers the audio callbacks.
evidence: Sound_InitSystem (0x001EB880) calls it during startup and Sound_PlayerSlot_Clear (0x005EA4F0) operates on the same slot table, which pins it to sound-system initialisation.

name: Menu_UpdateSelectionPage
signature: unsigned Menu_UpdateSelectionPage(MenuState* self, unsigned* out, unsigned handle, unsigned count1, unsigned count2, int mode)
summary: Evaluates the menu's entry selection page: builds the candidate list, resolves the current entry, applies the page/limit rules and writes the chosen actor and sub-slot back to the caller.
evidence: The named callers Menu_ResolveSelectedEntryActors (0x0020605C), Menu_SelectRecipeRow (0x00202C50) and Battle_SelectAiActions (0x0016C7F8) all use it to turn a cursor position into the selected entry.

name: maybe_Menu_TestEntryCondition
signature: unsigned char maybe_Menu_TestEntryCondition(MenuState* self, int entryTable, int index)
summary: Tests the per-entry condition byte at entryTable+0x205+index*2: case 1/2 compare the actor's HP/MP ratio with the threshold, case 3 tests a status bit, later cases count party members, and it returns whether the entry is usable.
evidence: The new callers (Menu_SelectRecipeRow 0x00202C50, Menu_UpdateSelectionPage 0x002031A4) and the four distinct case branches show that only cases 1-2 are ratio tests; calling the whole function 'RatioCondition' was wrong.

name: Menu_CreateEntryObjects
summary: Creates the menu's per-entry objects (0x68 of them) on the +0x4308 list and initialises the metadata block at +0x56C4.
evidence: Maybe_Menu_InitFromParams (0x0020713C) calls it while building the menu, and the body's 0x68-iteration allocation loop matches the entry count.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyStatusWindow_CommitRows
signature: void maybe_Ui_PartyStatusWindow_CommitRows(PartyStatusWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Thumb copy of the four-row member commit: collects the ids of the first four rows, removes duplicates and rewrites the party member table through func_00612ADC(work+0x24A98).
evidence: Damaged decompilation (unaff_r4/r5/r6/r7/r8/r9/r10 and a stack-relative self), so the argument registers and thus the exact row range cannot be confirmed; the dedup + party-table write is visible.

name: BattleScene_UpdateState
summary: State machine of the battle scene: dispatches the per-state update/setup routines for states 0..7 and hides the two helper list widgets (work+0x4254/+0x4270) when a state does not need them.
evidence: The switch body now calls the confidently named BattleScene_LayoutPartyModels, BattleScene_UpdateScreenState0Main/1/2, BattleScene_UpdateUnitModelTransforms and BattleScene_AdjustUnitModelTransform, so both the role and the state dispatch are pinned.

name: maybe_BattleScene_UpdateScreenState0
summary: Small entry point that flows into the battle-scene state-0 update at 0x00609498 (BattleScene_UpdateScreenState0Main); it shares the literal pool constant 0x00609988 with that function.
evidence: The symbol is only 24 bytes, so the readable body cannot be its own code - Ghidra followed the fallthrough into 0x00609498, whose name is already confident. The split point/role is plausible but the name would be misleading.

name: Menu_UpdateSelectionWindow
summary: Updates the multi-member selection window: builds the per-selection objects, refreshes the actor list and closes the window when the selection completes.
evidence: Its own subroutine Menu_TeardownWindow (0x0020F948) calls it, and the body's battle-flag check (work+0x4244) plus the lazily allocated 0x21C object match a battle selection window.

name: maybe_Ui_RebuildParts
signature: void maybe_Ui_RebuildParts(Window* self, const u8* desc, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Rebuilds a window's part list from a layout descriptor: releases the previous parts (f_CC/f_D0) and recreates them with the 0x002F7528/0x002F7590 part builder.
evidence: Callees are now named (Mem_AllocAligned_2, func_002F7658/002F7590/002F7528) and the release/rebuild order is clear, but the body is damaged (unaff_r9, dropped argument registers) and no named caller proves the class.

name: Ui_Overlay_ClearAll
signature: void Ui_Overlay_ClearAll(UiOverlay* self, const u8* mode)
summary: Full reset of the overlay manager: destroys both child sprite layers, blanks the twelve slot widgets (keeping slots 8 and 9), resets the cached per-slot ids and releases every live marker through its element's virtual release.
evidence: The body now calls the named Ui_Overlay_ClearEntries plus Field_DetachSlotObjectA/B on gameWork+0x54 and walks the slot table exactly as described; the callers include Field_ExitTalkMode.

name: Actor_UpdateActionState
summary: Refreshes an actor's action state from the overlay state bytes at +0x27C/+0x27F/+0x281, choosing model scale/anchor values and applying them to the actor.
evidence: It is called from the named Actor_ApplyMoveCommand, Actor_SelectIdleAnimation, Actor_CreateActionTable, Party_Status_SelectPage and Ui_OverlaySlot_ApplyStateChange, i.e. after every action/state change.

name: Ui_Overlay_HideElementClass
summary: Clears the overlay manager's second visibility flag and asks every registered element of one class to hide itself (the hide half of the show/hide pair).
evidence: Body: f_285 = 0, then the registry walk on gameWork+0x54 with the class mask 0x40000040 and a per-element hide call; the mirror at 0x0023A580 sets f_285 = 1, which pins the polarity.

name: Ui_Overlay_CreateAuxWidget
signature: u32 Ui_Overlay_CreateAuxWidget(UiOverlay* self, const u8* slot)
summary: Creates the auxiliary widget for the selected overlay slot (kinds 1..7, stored at +0x20..+0x38) from that slot's sprite record and marks the element as needing a re-place.
evidence: The body switches on the slot kind and constructs the matching widget (0x002B6A08/0x0021B86C/0x002B6AB4/...), then sets element->f_59A = 1; called from the named Ui_OverlaySlot_ApplyStateChange path.

name: maybe_Field_Marker_QueueSystemCommand
summary: Posts a system command (id 8) to the field command queue after building the argument block, bailing out while the event task slot is busy.
evidence: The 0x24A98 arena and func_00613354(...,8,...) are clear, but the 0x55555555-popcount inline and the damaged register flow leave the 'marker' subject and the exact arguments unproven.

name: Actor_RebuildCharacterModel
summary: Rebuilds an actor's character model after a character/outfit change: resolves the character table, applies the entry's size/offset to the model object f_B8, resets the transform controller f_BC and unregisters the old model id.
evidence: The body uses the named character-table accessors and func_0023D078 player index, and its caller Ui_OverlaySlot_ApplyStateChange re-runs it whenever the displayed character changes.

name: Ui_DragScroll_Begin
signature: UiDragScroll* Ui_DragScroll_Begin(UiDragScroll* drag, UiListWindow* list, int useTouch)
summary: Starts a drag-scroll: copies the start point from the list, records the pointer id and the UI mode, sets state 1 and disables list input while dragging.
evidence: The body writes drag[0]/[1] from list[0x88]/[0x89], state = 1, calls the now-named Ui_Overlay_ShowElementClass and then the list's vtable+0x58(4) to lock input.

name: ModelPreview_UpdateAttachments
summary: Refreshes a model preview's attachment/effect set: rebuilds the per-state parts and effects, plays the slot's animation and shows/hides the attachment slots according to the preview state.
evidence: Callees are now named (maybe_Effect_FindOrCreateInstance, Model_AttachSlot_ShowAll/HideAll via func_002219C8/func_0022225C) and it is called by ModelPreview_SelectSlot (0x002351B4) and Actor_ResetStateModelIfCurrent.

name: Actor_InitStateModels
summary: Initialises an actor's per-state models: sets the model visibility flags, plays the initial action and creates the effect/mesh part for every state the inventory/state tables report.
evidence: The body calls the now-named Field_SceneNode_NotifyChildrenUpdate, func_005E74A0/func_00233738 (initial action) and func_00636000 (inventory-flag test) per state, then creates the per-state part at self+i*4+0x420.

name: Field_Actor_UpdateWeaponAttach
summary: Per-frame weapon attachment: when the weapon id is active it binds the 'Attach' node, computes the weapon's world matrix from the hand node and stores it on the actor.
evidence: String literal 'Attach' at 0x003E8A28 plus the now-named Gfx_Model_AttachGadgetMesh/Anim_ActionSeq_StartForActor calls make the attachment role explicit; the Range variant at 0x003E8D48 is its sibling.

name: Actor_UpdateFollowTarget
summary: Per-frame follow update: compares the actor position with the follow target, plays the walk/run animation depending on the state flag, and clears the follow offset when the actor is inside the arrival radius.
evidence: The body's target fields (+0x3D4..+0x3DC vs actor +0x9C..+0xA4), vtable+0x68/+0x6C animation switch and f_C4 reset match, and 0x003DD3E0 (UpdateFollowTargetMotion) is the continuation.

name: Model_ApplyFacingTilt
signature: u32 Model_ApplyFacingTilt(ModelNode* self, const float* dir)
summary: Moves a model node along a direction and, depending on the tilt mode (+0x74), snaps it to the world axes or rotates it toward the direction, then selects the 'Ascent'/'Decent' animation state.
evidence: String literals s_Ascent/s_Decent plus the named Math_QuatFromAxisAngle (0x005755C8) call confirm the rotation path; the direction accumulation at +0x100..+0x108 is verified.

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_NotifyChildren
summary: Forwards a value to two attached children: calls a per-child handler on f_220 (no argument) and then on f_160 with the given value.
evidence: The callee is currently named Anim_ActionSeq_StartForActor, which is clearly a misnomer for a generic per-node notify, so neither the verb nor the 'SceneNode' class is trustworthy here.

name: Script_LoadEventScript
signature: u32 Script_LoadEventScript(EventState* self, int mode, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Loads the script/message data an event needs: pulls script_message.bxon and cs_text.bxon from the message archive, finds the .cnut script object and applies it to every actor slot according to the mode selector.
evidence: String literals s_script_message_bxon/s_cs_text_bxon/s_script_cnut plus Script_RunScriptFile (0x00579D20) and Container_FindObjectByClassAndNameB (0x00713AF4) are the named callees; mode <0/1/2 select all/first/last slot.

name: Event_LoadScenarioPack
signature: void Event_LoadScenarioPack(EventState* self, const u8* mode, const u16* ids)
summary: Prepares a scenario/cutscene event: resolves the scenario pack name from the map/event id, loads 'param/scenario_cs*.pack', binds the 54 resource names into the script object and selects the event, the CS viewer or the scenario entry depending on the mode.
evidence: Literal s_param_scenario_cs__s_pack_00254aa8, the 0x36-entry resource loop and the named Script_LoadScriptPack (0x0028DF58) match; the mode byte is tested against 0/1/2/5/7.

name: Text_ExecuteCommand
signature: void Text_ExecuteCommand(TextCommandState* self, u32 command, int restoreCursor)
summary: Executes one text/talk control command: saves the current character, dispatches through the eight-entry handler table, refreshes the text window for commands that change the layout and restores the cursor.
evidence: Text_CommandHandler0's own header documents the eight static handlers at 0x0072C5B8 (0x257D1C..0x257F6C) and states that this function copies that table and dispatches on an index 0..7, then renders the text buffer at +0x24 - an independent confirmation of the role.

name: Text_SetCommandArgs
signature: void Text_SetCommandArgs(TextCommandState* self, const void* args, u8 count)
summary: Stores the argument block and argument count used by the next text command.
evidence: Body is a 0x84-byte std_memcpy into self->f_24 plus self->f_12D = count; the Text_CommandHandler0 header names 0x00257DB0 as the function that fills that 0x84-byte argument buffer and 0x00257B30 as the dispatcher that passes it to the window renderer.

name: maybe_Actor_ActionSeq_RunChoice2
signature: * maybe_Actor_ActionSeq_RunChoice2 - Action-sequence step for a longer branch node: it reads the current * step result (func_0064DF08) and either retries with action 0 (when the step reported failure), or marks * the runner done (f_4fd4) and requests action 0, storing the new step id. * * Recovered: N_025, confidence 0.40, address 0x002E9CD0 (arm, 0 bytes). * Signature: u32 maybe_Actor_ActionSeq_RunChoice2(ActorActionSeq* self) * Evidence: `f4fcc = self->f_4fcc; if ((f4fcc & 0x142)==0)
summary: Action-sequence step for a longer branch node: reads the current step result (func_0064DF08) and either retries with action 0 or marks the runner done and stores the new step id.
evidence: The f_4FCC flag tests (0x142/4/1) and f_2AC vtable+0x3C call are verified, but the same shape appears in 0x004A1704 and no named caller identifies which action sequence this is.

name: maybe_Ui_ProfileWindow_CopySubState
summary: Copies two small sub-object states of a window (at +0x274 and +0x29C) from a source object.
evidence: Two func_0031893C calls with and without a source are verified, but the function is only 9 lines and no named caller proves it belongs to the profile window.

name: maybe_Ui_CommandPanel_UpdateSelection
summary: Runs the window's embedded choice sub-widget: releases its sub-widgets, calls the widget's vtable+0x3C with the stored arguments and compares the returned id with the stored selection.
evidence: Same code shape as maybe_Actor_ActionSeq_RunChoice2 (0x002E9CD0) - f_D80 bit tests 0x142/4, func_0064DF08 - so it is a choice/action runner, but 'CommandPanel' is not proven.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleTargetWindow_Init
signature: void maybe_Ui_BattleTargetWindow_Init(TargetWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 mode)
summary: Initialises the four target panes and the shared state label of the battle target window (resets cursors, clears the pane widgets and formats the state text), then resets the shown targets in normal mode.
evidence: Ghidra reports 'bad instruction data' and the body branches on f_34D0, so parts of the initialisation are missing; the four-pane loop and the named Battle_HpGaugeWindow_* calls are the only trustworthy evidence.

name: Ui_BattleTargetWindow_HideAlt
summary: Second copy of the battle target window's hide routine: when the window is shown it sets it invisible and releases the 0x1314 layout object.
evidence: Body is byte-identical to Ui_BattleTargetWindow_Hide (0x002695DC) and the named Battle_UiFlow_HideTargetWindow (0x002DE738) calls it, so 'HideAlt' correctly marks it as the duplicate vtable entry.

name: Ui_BattleTargetWindow_CloseIfNotEnemyTurn
signature: void Ui_BattleTargetWindow_CloseIfNotEnemyTurn(TargetWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Closes the target window unless the battle is in the enemy-turn state (+0x34D0 == 2), in which case it stays open while the enemies act.
evidence: The f_34D0 != 2 test, the SetStateVisible call and the 0x1314 release are verified, and the named callers Battle_FinishBattleScene, Menu_SelectPartyPair and BattleWindow_HideTargetWindow all close the window.

name: Ui_Window_EnsureChildObject
summary: Lazily creates the window's 0x6C-byte 2D scene object with the shared factory (name 0x007BE88E), attaches it with func_005E7650 and configures its four layout parameters; the handle is kept at f_36C.
evidence: The body is the same create-and-attach idiom as the two Gfx variants in this batch (0x002F9128, 0x002C12B0): Mem_AllocAligned_2(0x6C), Field_Object2D_CreateSceneEntry with 0x007BE88E, then attach. 'SubWindow_Init' named a class that the code does not show.

name: Gfx_SceneNode_EnsureChildObject
summary: Lazily creates a 0x6C-byte child scene object through the shared factory (name 0x007BE88E), stores it at f_390 and attaches it to the node.
evidence: Body: Mem_AllocAligned_2(0x6C) + std_FixedString15_Ctor(0x007BE88E) + Field_Object2D_CreateSceneEntry(...,self) + Model_Equip_CreateWeaponMeshes + func_005E7650(self,handle) - identical to 0x002C12B0/0x003E6110, so 'EnsureChildB' was a copy letter, not a name.

name: Gfx_SceneNode_EnsureChildObjectB
summary: Lazily creates and attaches a 0x6C-byte child scene object (shared factory name 0x007BE88E) at f_224 and then sets the render flags and synchronises the two flag bytes.
evidence: Same construction block as 0x002F9128/0x003E6110 with an extra Gfx_SceneNode_LoadMeshByName call and the flag sync at the end; 'InitChild' hid that it is the same ensure-child helper.

name: Ui_StoryModel_SelectPage
summary: Refreshes the 3D story model shown for the current page: clamps the page index, shows/hides the previous/next arrow widgets, formats 'ui_story/%s_%s_3d.bch' for the page's entry and loads that BCH through the shared model cache.
evidence: Literal s_ui_story__s_3d_bch, the per-index tables 0x0072A350/0x0072A360 and Ui_StoryListWindow_BindRowModels (0x001C38C4) sharing them confirm the role.

name: Gfx_Overlay_DrawScreenQuad
signature: void Gfx_Overlay_DrawScreenQuad(OverlayCtx* self, GfxCmd* cmd, int screen)
summary: Draws a full-screen textured quad for the top or bottom screen: picks 400x240 or 320x240 from the screen argument, builds the two vertices with the current Gfx scene transform, submits the copy commands and flushes.
evidence: Screen constants 0x1E0/0x140/400/0xF0 and the named Gfx_CmdBuf_AppendCommandList (0x00563DB0) plus the 0x0057D7B0..0x0057DFEC draw helpers pin the role.

name: Gfx_Overlay_DrawContent
signature: int* Gfx_Overlay_DrawContent(GfxOverlay* self, u32 x, u32 y)
summary: Draws the overlay content into the 320x240 top screen: sets up the destination rect, clamps the given position, binds the overlay texture and configures the two viewport/sub-rect structures when the wide flag is set.
evidence: Constants 0x140/0xF0 (=320x240), maybe_Gfx_GetRenderContext and Gfx_CopyBufferData (0x005642C8) are named, and the f_1346 'wide/3D offset' test matches 0x002D2D9C.

name: Gfx_Overlay_DrawMainScreen
signature: int* Gfx_Overlay_DrawMainScreen(OverlayCtx* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Main overlay draw pass: draws the 400x240 background quad, then the three sorted sub-lists, a sprite batch and the 0x100x0x200 scene rectangle when present.
evidence: Body walks the list heads f_FE8/f_FF4/f_1000/f_100C through the named Gfx_CmdBuf_AppendCommandList and Gfx_CopyBufferData; the constants 0x100/0x200 are the scene rectangle.

name: maybe_Gfx_Overlay_DrawMainScreenB
summary: Second variant of the main overlay draw pass: the same 0x2D2930/0x2D31B0/0x2D4484 submission sequence plus 0x0055DC6C, used when the overlay mode differs from 0x002D36C8.
evidence: The body is damaged (coprocessor_load(7,...), in_cr0/in_cr8, overlapping instructions at 0x2D43A0), so the exact variant behaviour cannot be confirmed; only the shared callee set is clear.
